claims.source: The defect in myotube formation caused by knockdown of endogenous mouse Pask was reversed by the expression of siRNA-resistant human wild type (WT) Pask, but not a K1028R kinase-dead (KD) Pask mutant (Figure 1C, quantified in Figure 1D, Figure 1—source data 1) (Kikani et al., 2010), indicating the necessity of Pask catalytic activity for myoblast fusion.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the rescue experiment showing only catalytically active Pask can restore differentiation.

claims.claim: The effect of Pask on myoblast fusion is cell autonomous, as only cells expressing WT Pask show rescue of the fusion defect.
claims.source: Importantly, this effect appears to be cell autonomous as only that fraction of cells in the population that express WT Pask (WT+) show rescue of the fusion defect, whereas cells not expressing hPask within the same culture (WT-) remained mono-nucleated and fusion defective.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data showing differential effects within the same culture based on Pask expression.

claims.claim: Mylpf (myosin light chain) and Acta1 mRNAs fail to be induced in Pask knockdown cells during differentiation.
claims.source: Additionally, Mylpf (myosin light chain) and Acta1 mRNAs, which are both markers of myoblast differentiation, failed to be induced in Pask knockdown cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Expression of both Mylpf and Acta1 genes is rescued by expression of WT but not KD human PASK in Pask knockdown cells.
claims.source: Expression of both genes was rescued by expression of WT but not KD human PASK (Figure 1E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E.

claims.claim: Neither genetic deletion nor inhibition of Pask has any effect on the proliferation rate of primary myoblasts under proliferative culture conditions.
claims.source: Under proliferative culture conditions, neither genetic deletion nor inhibition of Pask had any effect on the proliferation rate (Figure 1—figure supplement 4F, Figure 1—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by cell proliferation data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4F.

claims.claim: Genetic elimination of Pask (myoblasts derived from germline Pask-/- mice) causes a ~60% decrease in differentiation efficiency of primary myoblasts.
claims.source: In response to differentiation cues, myoblasts derived from WT mice efficiently formed multi-nucleated myotubes (Figure 1F, quantified in Figure 1G). In contrast, genetic elimination of Pask (i.e. myoblasts derived from germline Pask-/- mice) caused a ~60% decrease in differentiation efficiency.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 1F-G.

claims.claim: The effect of Pask inhibition in WT primary myoblasts is more pronounced than genetic deletion, almost completely eliminating myotube formation.
claims.source: Interestingly, the effect of Pask inhibition in WT cells was much more pronounced, almost completely eliminating myotube formation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 1F-G comparing genetic deletion and pharmacological inhibition.

claims.claim: BioE-1197 has no effect on Pask-/- myoblasts, demonstrating that the effects of the BioE-1197 Pask inhibitor are completely dependent on the presence of Pask.
claims.source: BioE-1197 had no effect, however, on Pask-/- myoblasts (Figure 1F, quantified in Figure 1G). This result demonstrates that the effects of the BioE-1197 Pask inhibitor are completely dependent on the presence of Pask, a clear indication that these effects are mediated by Pask inhibition.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 1F-G demonstrating specificity of the inhibitor.

claims.claim: Myoblasts derived from germline Pask-/- mice exhibit a Pask-independent compensation that partially rescues myotube formation in vitro.
claims.source: Moreover, these results demonstrate that myoblasts derived from germline Pask-/- mice exhibit a Pask-independent compensation that appears, at least in vitro, to partially rescue myotube formation.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that genetic deletion has a less severe phenotype than acute inhibition.

claims.claim: The myoblast differentiation process is activated in vivo to repair and replenish the myotome after muscle injury.
claims.source: The myoblast differentiation process is activated in vivo to repair and replenish the myotome after muscle injury.
claims.evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about muscle regeneration.

claims.claim: During muscle regeneration, satellite cells become activated, proliferate and eventually fuse in response to differentiating signals to restore mature myotubes.
claims.source: During muscle regeneration, satellite cells become activated, proliferate and eventually fuse in response to differentiating signals to restore mature myotubes.
claims.evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about muscle regeneration.

claims.claim: PASK mRNA and protein expression is robustly upregulated as early as 3 days post muscle injury.
claims.source: We observed that as early as 3 days post injury, PASK mRNA (Figure 1H, Figure 1—source data 1) and protein (Figure 1I) expression was robustly upregulated.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR and Western blot data shown in Figure 1H-I.

claims.claim: High Pask expression during muscle regeneration is consistent with high Pask expression in stem cells compared with differentiated cells, since muscle stem cells begin to proliferate upon muscle injury.
claims.source: This is consistent with high Pask expression in stem cells compared with differentiated cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), since muscle stem cells begin to proliferate upon muscle injury before eventually fusing to replenish the injured myotome.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the correlation between Pask expression patterns in stem cells and during regeneration.

claims.claim: Myh3, a marker of regenerative myogenesis, is robustly induced as early as Day 5 post-injury in WT animals, but Pask-/- animals show very little induction of Myh3 expression.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 1I, whereas Myh3, a marker of regenerative myogenesis, was robustly induced as early as Day 5 in WT animals, Pask-/- animals showed very little induction of Myh3 expression.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 1I.

claims.claim: WT animals show robust induction of Myh3 immunohistochemical staining during muscle regeneration, but this is blunted in Pask-/- muscle.
claims.source: Similarly, WT animals show robust induction of Myh3 immunohistochemical staining, but this was blunted in Pask-/- muscle (Figure 1J, quantified in Figure 1K).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunohistochemistry and quantification data shown in Figure 1J-K.

claims.claim: Mammalian Pask plays an important role in the differentiation of stem cells across many lineages in vitro and during muscle regeneration in vivo.
claims.source: Taken together, our data suggest that mammalian Pask plays an important role in the differentiation of stem cells across many lineages in vitro and during muscle regeneration in vivo.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from all the differentiation experiments across multiple cell types and the in vivo regeneration data.

claims.claim: Following injury, satellite cells execute a transcriptional program that culminates in the formation of syncytial myocytes that constitute a healthy muscle fiber.
claims.source: Following injury, satellite cells execute a transcriptional program that culminates in the formation of syncytial myocytes that constitute a healthy muscle fiber (Figure 2A) (Bentzinger et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Bentzinger et al., 2012) and represents established knowledge.

claims.claim: Quiescent Pair Box 7+ (Pax7+) satellite cells are induced to proliferate and initiate expression of Myoblast Determination protein (MyoD) and/or Myogenic Factor 5 (Myf5) during muscle regeneration.
claims.source: Quiescent Pair Box 7+ (Pax7+) satellite cells are induced to proliferate and initiate expression of Myoblast Determination protein (MyoD) and/orMyogenic Factor 5(Myf5).
claims.evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about the myogenic transcriptional cascade.

claims.claim: In MyoD+ myoblasts, MyoD drives the expression of Myogenin (MyoG) in response to differentiation cues.
claims.source: In MyoD+ myoblasts, MyoD drives the expression of Myogenin (MyoG) in response to differentiation cues.
claims.evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about the myogenic transcriptional cascade.

claims.claim: MyoG executes the terminal differentiation program by down-regulating Pax7 expression and activating the genes necessary for myoblast fusion and muscle function, including myosin heavy chain (Mylpf) and muscle specific actin (Acta1).
claims.source: MyoG then executes the terminal differentiation program by down-regulating Pax7 expression (Olguin and Olwin, 2004) and activating the genes necessary for myoblast fusion and muscle function, including myosin heavy chain (Mylpf) and muscle specific actin (Acta1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Olguin and Olwin, 2004) and represents established knowledge.

claims.claim: The abundance of Pax7 and Myf5 mRNAs declines at day 1 of differentiation in WT satellite cells.
claims.source: As expected, the abundance of the Pax7 and Myf5 mRNAs declined at day 1 of differentiation in WT cells (Figure 2B, Figure 2—source data 1) (Bentzinger et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Myog mRNA abundance increases at Day 1 of differentiation in WT satellite cells, as does expression of its target genes Mylpf and Acta1.
claims.source: In conjunction, Myog mRNA abundance increased at Day 1, as did expression of its target genes Mylpf and Acta1 (Figure 2B, Figure 2—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Pask-/- satellite cells exhibit, even at Day 0, a more satellite cell-like gene expression profile, with Pax7 and Myf5 being elevated relative to WT and Myog and its targets Mylpf and Acta1 having decreased expression.
claims.source: Pask-/- cells exhibited, even at Day 0, a more satellite cell-like gene expression profile, with Pax7 and Myf5 being elevated relative to WT and Myog and its targets Mylpf and Acta1 having decreased expression.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: At Day 1 of differentiation, Pask-/- satellite cells maintain elevated Pax7 and Myf5 mRNAs and decreased Myog, Mylpf and Acta1 expression.
claims.source: At Day 1 of differentiation, these patterns were maintained, with Pax7 and Myf5 mRNAs remaining elevated and Myog, Mylpf and Acta1 remaining decreased (Figure 2B, Figure 2—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: The expression of Myod is not affected by the loss of Pask in satellite cells.
claims.source: The expression of Myod, on the other hand, was not affected by the loss of Pask.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2B.

claims.claim: Pask-/- animals show a profound defect in the induction of MyoG and its target Myh3 during in vivo muscle regeneration.
claims.source: Pask-/- animals also showed a profound defect in the induction of MyoG and its target Myh3 (Figure 2C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2C.

claims.claim: At Day 1 of differentiation, when Pask silencing is most effective, Pax7 abundance remains elevated and the induction of the early differentiation marker MyoG and its target MHC is delayed in Pask-silenced C2C12 cells.
claims.source: At Day 1 of differentiation, when Pask silencing was most effective, Pax7 abundance remained elevated and the induction of the early differentiation marker MyoG and its target MHC was delayed in Pask-silenced C2C12 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claims.claim: Pask inhibition by BioE-1197 recapitulates the effects of Pask silencing on Pax7, MyoG, and MHC expression at the mRNA level during insulin-induced C2C12 differentiation.
claims.source: Pask inhibition by BioE-1197 recapitulated these effects at the mRNA level during insulin-induced C2C12 differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Transcriptional defects in myogenesis caused by Pask knockdown are rescued by ectopic expression of human WT but not kinase dead (KD) Pask.
claims.source: These transcriptional defects in myogenesis caused by Pask knockdown were rescued by ectopic expression of human WT but not kinase dead (KD) Pask (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Pask is required to initiate the commitment phase of myoblast differentiation and maintain the myogenic transcriptional program.
claims.source: Taken together, our findings suggest that Pask is required to initiate the commitment phase of myoblast differentiation and maintain the myogenic transcriptional program.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from the gene expression and differentiation data.

claims.claim: At Day 0, ~40% of control C2C12 cells are Pax7+ and this fraction declines over the course of differentiation.
claims.source: At Day 0, ~40% of control cells were Pax7+ and this fraction declined over the course of differentiation (Figure 2D, quantified in 2E, Figure 2—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 2D-E.

claims.claim: When Pask is inhibited or knocked down, the number of Pax7+ cells is elevated at Day 0 and during differentiation.
claims.source: When Pask was inhibited or knocked down, the number of Pax7+ cells was elevated at Day 0 and during differentiation, matching the mRNA data (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 1A–B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2D-E.

claims.claim: Pask knockdown or inhibition has no effect on the number or subcellular localization of MyoD at any point during C2C12 differentiation.
claims.source: In contrast, Pask knockdown or inhibition had no effect on the number or subcellular localization of MyoD at any point during differentiation, consistent with Figure 2B (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A, quantified in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A-B.

claims.claim: In control C2C12 cells, the fraction of MyoG+ cells dramatically increases from Day 0 (~7%) to Day 1 (~60%) and Day 2 (~80%).
claims.source: In control cells, the fraction of MyoG+ cells dramatically increased from Day 0 (~7%) to Day 1 (~60%) and Day 2 (~80%) (Figure 2F, quantified in 2G, Figure 2—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 2F-G.

claims.claim: MyoG+ cell numbers are substantially reduced by either Pask inhibition or knockdown during C2C12 differentiation.
claims.source: MyoG+ cell numbers were substantially reduced by either Pask inhibition or knockdown.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 2F-G.

claims.claim: At Day 1 of C2C12 differentiation, there is a strong co-expression between Pask and MyoG, wherein ~50% of Pask+ cells are MyoG+ whereas only ~15% of Pask- cells are MyoG+.
claims.source: We also noticed a striking correlation of Pask and MyoG expression. At Day 1, we observed a strong co-expression between Pask and MyoG, wherein ~50% of Pask+ cells were MyoG+ whereas only ~15% of Pask- cells were MyoG+ (Figure 2F, quantified in Figure 2H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 2F and 2H.

claims.claim: Inhibition of Pask function with BioE-1197 eliminates the correlation between Pask and MyoG expression, with both Pask+ and Pask- populations losing MyoG staining.
claims.source: As expected, inhibition of Pask function with BioE-1197 eliminated this correlation, with both populations losing MyoG staining.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2F and quantified in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: In Pask knockdown samples, MyoG expression is present almost exclusively in those cells in the population that escaped Pask silencing.
claims.source: Importantly, in the Pask knockdown samples, MyoG expression was present almost exclusively in those cells in the population that escaped Pask silencing (Figure 2F, quantified in Figure 2H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 2F and quantified in Figure 2H.

claims.claim: Both the increase in Pax7+ cells and the decrease in MyoG+ cells observed upon Pask knockdown are completely rescued by expression of WT hPask.
claims.source: Both the increase in Pax7+ cells and the decrease in MyoG+ cells observed upon Pask knockdown were completely rescued by expression of WT hPask (Figure 2I, quantified in Figure 2J).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 2I-J.

claims.claim: Transient over-expression of human Pask, even in the absence of extrinsic differentiation cues, is sufficient to induce formation of multi-nucleated myocytes.
claims.source: Surprisingly, transient over-expression of human Pask, even in the absence of extrinsic differentiation cues, was sufficient to induce formation of multi-nucleated myocytes (Figure 2K) and to induce the entire differentiation transcriptional program in growth medium (GM) (Figure 2L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 2K.

claims.claim: Transient over-expression of human Pask in growth medium induces the entire differentiation transcriptional program, including suppression of Pax7 as well as induction of Myod, Myog and Mylpf.
claims.source: Surprisingly, transient over-expression of human Pask, even in the absence of extrinsic differentiation cues, was sufficient to induce formation of multi-nucleated myocytes (Figure 2K) and to induce the entire differentiation transcriptional program in growth medium (GM) (Figure 2L). This included suppression of Pax7 as well as induction of Myod, Myog and Mylpf.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2L.

claims.claim: Addition of differentiation medium (DM) further enhances myoblast differentiation in hPask-expressing cells, as evidenced by the elevated expression of Myog and Mylpf.
claims.source: Addition of differentiation medium (DM) further enhanced myoblast differentiation in hPask-expressing cells, as evidenced by the elevated expression of Myog and Mylpf (Figure 2L).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 2L.

claims.claim: Pask is necessary for the timely execution of the terminal differentiation program in myoblasts and is sufficient to initiate that program even in the absence of extrinsic differentiation signals.
claims.source: Together, these data establish Pask as necessary for the timely execution of the terminal differentiation program in myoblasts and as sufficient to initiate that program even in the absence of extrinsic differentiation signals.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from the loss-of-function and gain-of-function experiments.

claims.claim: MyoG and MyoD occupy the Pask promoter during C2C12 differentiation coincident with H3K4me3 modification and RNA-PolII recruitment.
claims.source: Interestingly, previous ChIP-Seq data had suggested that MyoG, and to a lesser extent MyoD, occupies the Pask promoter during C2C12 differentiation coincident with H3K4me3 modification and RNA-PolII recruitment (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A) (Yue et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data from Yue et al., 2014 shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A.

claims.claim: MyoG is recruited to the proximal Pask promoter upon initiation of differentiation.
claims.source: We independently validated that MyoG was indeed recruited to the proximal Pask promoter upon initiation of differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B) and that MyoG expression stimulates expression from a Pask promoter-driven reporter gene (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3B.

claims.claim: MyoG expression stimulates expression from a Pask promoter-driven reporter gene.
claims.source: We independently validated that MyoG was indeed recruited to the proximal Pask promoter upon initiation of differentiation (Figure 2—figure supplement 3B) and that MyoG expression stimulates expression from a Pask promoter-driven reporter gene (Figure 2—figure supplement 3C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase reporter assay data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3C.

claims.claim: Pask expression in differentiating myoblasts might be driven by MyoG to further support commitment to differentiate.
claims.source: These data suggest the possibility that Pask expression in differentiating myoblasts might be driven by MyoG to further support commitment to differentiate.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing MyoG binds to and activates the Pask promoter.

claims.claim: Pask and MyoG engage in a positive, self-reinforcing feedback loop to enforce the terminal differentiation program once it has been signaled to initiate.
claims.source: Thus, taken together, our data show that Pask and MyoG engage in a positive, self-reinforcing feedback loop to enforce the terminal differentiation program once it has been signaled to initiate.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the data showing Pask promotes MyoG expression and MyoG promotes Pask expression.

claims.claim: MyoD is a pioneering transcription factor that is sufficient to induce a myogenic cell fate even in non-muscle progenitor cells.
claims.source: MyoD is a pioneering transcription factor that is sufficient to induce a myogenic cell fate even in non-muscle progenitor cells.
claims.evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about MyoD function.

claims.claim: C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal stem cells normally express the Peroxisome proliferator-receptor activated gamma 2 (PPARγ2) adipogenic transcription factor and efficiently differentiate into adipocytes in response to adipogenic differentiation cues.
claims.source: C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal stem cells normally express the Peroxisome proliferator-receptor activated gamma 2 (PPARγ2) adipogenic transcription factor and efficiently differentiate into adipocytes in response to adipogenic differentiation cues (Figure 3A, ) (Zhao et al., 2013).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Zhao et al., 2013) and represents established knowledge.

claims.claim: The myogenic transcriptional program is epigenetically silenced in C3H10T1/2 cells, but it can be activated in response to MyoD expression.
claims.source: The myogenic transcriptional program is epigenetically silenced in C3H10T1/2 cells, but it can be activated in response to MyoD expression (Penn et al., 2004; Tapscott et al., 1988).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Penn et al., 2004; Tapscott et al., 1988).

claims.claim: In C3H10T1/2 cells, MyoD stimulates MyoG expression, which then collaborates with MyoD to establish myogenic commitment and repress Pparγ2 expression.
claims.source: MyoD stimulates MyoG expression, which then collaborates with MyoD to establish myogenic commitment and repress Pparγ2 expression (Figure 3A).
claims.evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about MyoD-induced myogenic conversion.

claims.claim: MyoD-induced expression of Myog and Mylpf is impaired by Pask inhibition in C3H10T1/2 cells while MyoD expression is unaffected.
claims.source: As shown in Figure 3B, MyoD-induced expression of Myog and Mylpf was impaired by Pask inhibition while MyoD expression was unaffected.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: Pparγ2 expression, which is lost in control C3H10T1/2 cells due to myogenic lineage conversion, is maintained in cells treated with BioE-1197.
claims.source: Moreover, Pparγ2 expression, which was lost in control cells due to myogenic lineage conversion, was maintained in cells treated with BioE-1197 (Figure 3B, Figure 3—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claims.claim: The fraction of MyoG+ cells at either Day 1 or Day 2 of differentiation is markedly decreased by Pask inhibition in MyoD-expressing C3H10T1/2 cells, while MyoD positivity is unaffected.
claims.source: In addition, as assessed by immunofluorescence microscopy, the fraction of MyoG+ cells at either Day 1 or Day 2 of differentiation was markedly decreased by Pask inhibition, while MyoDpositivity was unaffected (Figure 3C, quantified in Figure 3D; Figure 3—figure supplement 1A–B, Figure 3—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 3C-D and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A-B.

claims.claim: Cells treated with BioE-1197 exhibit a profound failure in the formation of multi-nucleated myotubes in the MyoD-induced myogenic conversion system.
claims.source: In addition to the loss of MyoG expression, cells treated with BioE-1197 exhibited a profound failure in the formation of multi-nucleated myotubes (Figure 3E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 3E.

claims.claim: The differentiation failure of Pask-inhibited C3H10T1/2 cells is not due to failed inactivation of Pax7, which is not expressed in C3H10T1/2 cells, but instead is due to an inability of MyoD to induce MyoG expression in the absence of Pask.
claims.source: Based on these results, we hypothesized that the differentiation failure of Pask-inhibited cells was not due to failed inactivation of Pax7, which is not expressed in C3H10T1/2 cells, but instead is due to an inability of MyoD to induce MyoG expression in the absence of Pask.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results in the C3H10T1/2 system which lacks Pax7.

claims.claim: Ectopic expression of rat MyoG is sufficient to bypass the Pask requirement for Mylpf expression even though endogenous mouse Myog remains suppressed in BioE-1197 treated C3H10T1/2 cells.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that ectopic expression of rat MyoG was sufficient to bypass the Pask requirement for Mylpf expression even though endogenous mouse Myog remained suppressed in BioE-1197 treated cells (Figure 3F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3F.

claims.claim: Pask acts within the myogenic transcriptional cascade, being necessary to act in concert with MyoD to induce MyoG expression and myogenic differentiation.
claims.source: These data place Pask within the myogenic transcriptional cascade, with Pask being necessary to act in concert with MyoD to induce MyoG expression and myogenic differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from the C3H10T1/2 experiments showing Pask is required for MyoD to induce MyoG.

claims.claim: Pask-dependent phosphorylation of one or more specific substrates is required for myogenic gene expression and differentiation.
claims.source: Catalytically inactive Pask was unable to rescue the differentiation defect caused by silencing of endogenous Pask (see Figure 1C–E, Figure 2—figure supplement 2C) and a catalytic inhibitor mimicked genetic inactivation of Pask (Figures 1A, 2F–G). We concluded, therefore, that Pask-dependent phosphorylation of one or more specific substrates must be required for the myogenic gene expression and differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the requirement for Pask catalytic activity in rescue experiments.

claims.claim: Wdr5 was identified as a candidate Pask substrate based on its interaction with Pask and containing the consensus phosphorylation motif for Pask ([HKR]-X-[KR]-X-X-[ST]).
claims.source: We employed a strategy that combines experimental and bioinformatics approaches. Specifically, we identified all proteins that had been described to physically interact with Pask in high-throughput protein-protein interactome datasets (BIOGRID: Pask) and were identified in our own unpublished Pask interactome studies. We then filtered this dataset for proteins that contain the consensus phosphorylation motif for Pask ([HKR]-X-[KR]-X-X-[ST]) that we previously identified (Kikani et al., 2010). Wdr5 was the single candidate substrate protein that emerged, based on its interaction with Pask in our dataset and in a global affinity capture screen (Ewing et al., 2007).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by bioinformatics analysis and citation to prior work (Kikani et al., 2010; Ewing et al., 2007).

claims.claim: Wdr5 associates with Pask during the proliferative phase of C2C12 cells, and this interaction is significantly enhanced following the onset of differentiation (Day 1).
claims.source: As shown in Figure 4A, Wdr5 associated with Pask during the proliferative phase (-1 and 0 days). However, that interaction was significantly enhanced following the onset of differentiation (Day 1) (Figure 4A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4A.

claims.claim: Co-expressed epitope-tagged forms of Pask and Wdr5 co-immunoprecipitate, and this does not require Pask catalytic activity as the K1028R Pask mutant (KD) precipitates Wdr5 equivalently to WT Pask.
claims.source: We also found that co-expressed epitope-tagged forms of Pask and Wdr5 co-immunoprecipitated and that this did not require Pask catalytic activity as the K1028R Pask mutant (KD) precipitated Wdr5 equivalently to WT Pask (Figure 4B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4B.

claims.claim: Wdr5 is a member of several protein complexes that catalyze histone methylation or acetylation.
claims.source: Wdr5 is a member of several protein complexes that catalyze histone methylation or acetylation (Migliori et al., 2012; Shilatifard, 2012; Trievel and Shilatifard, 2009).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Migliori et al., 2012; Shilatifard, 2012; Trievel and Shilatifard, 2009).

claims.claim: Among members of major Wdr5-containing complexes tested, only Wdr5 is able to co-purify endogenous Pask, suggesting that Pask is not a stable member of intact Wdr5-containing complexes, but might associate selectively with free Wdr5.
claims.source: Among these, only Wdr5 was able to co-purify endogenous Pask (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), suggesting that Pask is not a stable member of intact Wdr5-containing complexes, but might associate selectively with free Wdr5.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A and represents an inference from the data.

claims.claim: The interaction between Pask and Wdr5 appears to be direct as GST-tagged Wdr5, purified from bacteria, binds to Pask purified from insect cells.
claims.source: Supporting this notion, the interaction between Pask and Wdr5 appears to be direct as GST-tagged Wdr5, purified from bacteria, bound to Pask purified from insect cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GST pull-down data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: Wdr5 co-expression with Pask significantly enhances the nuclear accumulation of Pask, with nuclear Pask increasing from ~10% to a higher percentage of cells.
claims.source: Furthermore, while overexpressed Pask was cytoplasmic (typically perinuclear) in the majority of cells (Rutter et al., 2001), with only ~10% of cells exhibiting nuclear Pask in absence of Wdr5 co-expression, Wdr5 co-expression with Pask significantly enhanced the nuclear accumulation of Pask (Figure 4C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 4C.

claims.claim: The N-terminal 914 residues of Pask are dispensable for Wdr5 binding.
claims.source: We found that the N-terminal 914 residues of Pask were dispensable for Wdr5 binding (Figure 4—figure supplement 1C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data with Pask truncation mutants shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C.

claims.claim: Wdr5 likely interacts with Pask just upstream of the canonical protein kinase domain, as the interaction is lost upon deletion of residues 915–948.
claims.source: The interaction was lost, however, upon deletion of residues 915–948, suggesting that Wdr5 likely interacts with Pask just upstream of the canonical protein kinase domain.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data with Pask truncation mutants shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1C and represents an inference from the data.

claims.claim: Wdr5 is phosphorylated efficiently by WT Pask, but not KD Pask, in in vitro kinase reactions.
claims.source: Wdr5 was phosphorylated efficiently by WT Pask, but not KD Pask, in in vitro kinase reactions (Figure 4D) and this was abrogated by the BioE-1197 Pask inhibitor (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claims.claim: Wdr5 phosphorylation by Pask is abrogated by the BioE-1197 Pask inhibitor in in vitro kinase reactions.
claims.source: Wdr5 was phosphorylated efficiently by WT Pask, but not KD Pask, in in vitro kinase reactions (Figure 4D) and this was abrogated by the BioE-1197 Pask inhibitor (Figure 4—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: BioE-1197 robustly blunts the in situ phosphorylation of Pask and Pask-bound Wdr5 using in-cell 32P labeling.
claims.source: BioE-1197 also robustly blunted the in situ phosphorylation of Pask and Pask-bound Wdr5 using in-cell 32P labeling (Figure 4E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ phosphorylation data shown in Figure 4E.

claims.claim: Pask exhibits modest activity in the absence of stimulation in C2C12 myoblasts.
claims.source: Consistent with our previous report (Kikani et al., 2010), Pask exhibits modest activity in the absence of stimulation in C2C12 myoblasts (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 4F and citation to prior work (Kikani et al., 2010).

claims.claim: At 12 hr post-addition of insulin containing differentiation media, Pask is activated as assessed by increased autophosphorylation and Wdr5 phosphorylation.
claims.source: At 12 hr post-addition of insulin containing differentiation media, however, Pask was activated as assessed by increased autophosphorylation and Wdr5 phosphorylation, thus suggesting that Pask kinase activity is stimulated during differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 4F.

claims.claim: Pask kinase activity is stimulated during differentiation.
claims.source: At 12 hr post-addition of insulin containing differentiation media, however, Pask was activated as assessed by increased autophosphorylation and Wdr5 phosphorylation, thus suggesting that Pask kinase activity is stimulated during differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the increased Pask autophosphorylation and substrate phosphorylation upon differentiation.

claims.claim: The putative Pask phosphorylation site in Wdr5 with Serine 49 as the phospho-acceptor residue is strikingly similar to that of the best-characterized substrate of yeast Pask, Ugp1.
claims.source: That site, with Serine 49 as the putative phospho-acceptor residue, is strikingly similar to that of the best-characterized substrate of yeast Pask, Ugp1 (Figure 4G), which is also robustly phosphorylated by human Pask (Kikani et al., 2010; Rutter et al., 2002).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by sequence alignment shown in Figure 4G and citations to prior work (Kikani et al., 2010; Rutter et al., 2002).

claims.claim: The -5His and -3Lys residues in the Wdr5 phosphorylation motif are the most important for determining Pask phosphorylation.
claims.source: In particular, the -5His and -3Lys residues, which were shown to be the most important for determining Pask phosphorylation (Kikani et al., 2010), are present in this putative Wdr5 phosphorylation motif.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Kikani et al., 2010) that characterized the Pask consensus motif.

claims.claim: Ser49 is required for phosphorylation of Wdr5 by Pask since mutation to either glutamate (Glu) or alanine (Ala) nearly abolishes phosphorylation in vitro.
claims.source: As expected, we found that Ser49 is required for phosphorylation by Pask since mutation to either glutamate (Glu) or alanine (Ala) nearly abolished phosphorylation in vitro (Figure 4H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in vitro kinase assay data shown in Figure 4H.

claims.claim: Pask-associated WT Wdr5 is phosphorylated in cells, but the S49A mutant shows a marked reduction in 32P incorporation.
claims.source: Pask-associated WT Wdr5 was phosphorylated in cells as shown above, but the S49A mutant showed a marked reduction in 32P incorporation (Figure 4I).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by in situ phosphorylation data shown in Figure 4I.

claims.claim: Pask interacts with Wdr5 and phosphorylates it at Ser49 both in vitro and in cells.
claims.source: Together, these results suggest that Pask interacts with Wdr5 and phosphorylates it at Ser49 both in vitro and in cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary of the biochemical data showing Pask-Wdr5 interaction and phosphorylation.

claims.claim: Pask purified from insect cells binds to bacterial-expressed Wdr5S49E more weakly than WT, whereas Wdr5S49A binds Pask more avidly.
claims.source: Pask purified from insect cells bound to bacterial-expressed Wdr5S49E more weakly than WT, whereas Wdr5S49A bound Pask more avidly (Figure 4—figure supplement 1E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by GST pull-down data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1E.

claims.claim: The association of endogenous Pask with Wdr5 is weakened with Wdr5S49E and strengthened with Wdr5S49A compared with Wdr5WT in cells.
claims.source: A very similar pattern was observed in co-immunoprecipitation of endogenous Pask with Wdr5WT, WDRS49A and Wdr5S49E from cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1F). We found that the association with endogenous Pask is weakened with Wdr5S49E and strengthened with Wdr5S49A compared with Wdr5WT.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F.

claims.claim: An unphosphorylated substrate (mimicked by the Ala mutant) engages with its kinase with higher affinity compared to its phosphorylated forms (mimicked by the Glu mutant).
claims.source: These data are consistent with the common observation that an unphosphorylated substrate (mimicked by the Ala mutant) engages with its kinase with higher affinity compared to its phosphorylated forms (mimicked by the Glu mutant).
claims.evidence: This claim represents established knowledge about kinase-substrate interactions.

claims.claim: Wdr5WT, WDRS49A and Wdr5S49E all bind to each member of the Mll1-4, SET1 and KAT2a complexes equivalently, suggesting that Wdr5 phosphorylation by Pask does not alter recruitment of Wdr5 into its many chromatin-modifying complexes.
claims.source: When examining components of the Mll1-4, SET1 and KAT2a complexes, we found that Wdr5WT, WDRS49A and Wdr5S49E all bound to each member of these complexes equivalently, suggesting that Wdr5 phosphorylation by Pask does not alter recruitment of Wdr5 into its many chromatin-modifying complexes.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1F and represents an inference from the data.

claims.claim: Wdr5-containing complexes have a published role in myoblast differentiation via the regulation of myogenic gene expression.
claims.source: Having established Wdr5 as a Pask substrate and given the published role of Wdr5-containing complexes in myoblast differentiation via the regulation of myogenic gene expression (Asp et al., 2011; McKinnell et al., 2008; Segales et al., 2014), we wanted to determine whether Wdr5 phosphorylation is the mechanism through which Pask regulates Myog expression and myocyte differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Asp et al., 2011; McKinnell et al., 2008; Segales et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Expression of Wdr5S49E, but not Wdr5WT or Wdr5S49A, rescues the morphological features of C2C12 differentiation, including multinucleated myofibers.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that expression of Wdr5S49E, but not Wdr5WT or Wdr5S49A, rescued the morphological features of C2C12 differentiation, including multinucleated myofibers (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by microscopy data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claims.claim: Wdr5WT and Wdr5S49A have minimal effect on Pax7, Myog, Mylpf, or Acta1 mRNA abundance in Pask-siRNA C2C12 cells.
claims.source: Wdr5WT and Wdr5S49A had minimal effect on Pax7, Myog, Mylpf, or Acta1 mRNA abundance in Pask-siRNA cells (Figure 5A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Wdr5S49E either partially or completely rescues the defects in the expression of Pax7, Myog, Mylpf, and Acta1 genes caused by Pask knockdown.
claims.source: On the other hand, the Wdr5S49E mutant either partially or completely rescued the defects in the expression of each of these genes caused by Pask knockdown.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A.

claims.claim: Wdr5S49E causes a modest increase in Pask expression, likely due to the effects of increased MyoG activity on the Pask promoter.
claims.source: Wdr5S49E caused a modest increase in Pask expression, likely due to the effects of increased MyoG activity on the Pask promoter (Figure 2—figure supplement 2F–G).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 5A and represents an inference based on the MyoG-Pask feedback loop.

claims.claim: GFP, Wdr5WT, and Wdr5S49A have no significant effect on the number of Pax7+ cells in Pask-siRNA C2C12 cells.
claims.source: GFP, Wdr5WT, and Wdr5S49A all had no significant effect on the number of Pax7+ cells (Figure 5B; quantified in Figure 5C, Figure 5—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claims.claim: Wdr5S49E completely reverses the aberrant increase in Pax7+ cells caused by Pask knockdown.
claims.source: Wdr5S49E, on the other hand, completely reversed the aberrant increase in Pax7+ cells caused by Pask knockdown.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 5B-C.

claims.claim: The decrease in Pax7 positivity by Wdr5S49E is only present in those cells in the population that express Wdr5S49E (S49E+), and not in those cells that are uninfected (S49E-), demonstrating cell autonomous effects.
claims.source: Importantly, this decrease in Pax7 positivity was only present in those cells in the population that expressed Wdr5S49E (S49E+; Figure 5B, indicated by arrows), and not in those cells in the population that were uninfected (S49E-). This demonstrates that these are cell autonomous effects that are directly and specifically related to the expression of the phospho-mimetic Wdr5 mutant.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data shown in Figure 5B.

claims.claim: Cells expressing Wdr5S49E exhibit an almost complete rescue of MyoG expression in Pask knockdown cells, while those expressing GFP and Wdr5S49A are unaffected.
claims.source: Those cells expressing Wdr5S49E also exhibited an almost complete rescue of MyoGexpression, while those expressing GFP and Wdr5S49A were unaffected (Figure 5D; quantified in Figure 5E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claims.claim: Wdr5WT causes a significant increase in the fraction of MyoG+ cells in Pask knockdown C2C12 cells.
claims.source: In this case, Wdr5WT also caused a significant increase in the fraction of MyoG+ cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 5D-E.

claims.claim: MyoG expression is unaffected in those cells in the Wdr5WT and Wdr5S49E-expressing populations that are uninfected.
claims.source: As before, MyoG expression was unaffected in those cells in the Wdr5WT and Wdr5S49E-expressing populations that were uninfected.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy data showing cell autonomous effects.

claims.claim: The defect in MHC expression and myotube formation caused by Pask knockdown is robustly rescued in Wdr5S49E-expressing cells and weakly rescued in Wdr5WT-expressing cells.
claims.source: The defect in MHC expression and myotube formation caused by Pask knockdown was also robustly rescued in Wdr5S49E-expressing cells and weakly rescued in Wdr5WT-expressing cells (Figure 5F,G, Figure 5—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by immunofluorescence microscopy and quantification data shown in Figure 5F-G.

claims.claim: Ectopic expression of Wdr5S49E, like WT Pask, is sufficient to induce expression of MyoG even in the absence of differentiation stimuli.
claims.source: Furthermore, we noticed that ectopic expression of Wdr5S49E, like WT Pask, was sufficient to induce expression of MyoG even in the absence of differentiation stimuli (Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5H.

claims.claim: Expression of kinase-dead (KD) Pask, Wdr5WT or Wdr5S49A fails to induce MyoG expression in growth media.
claims.source: Expression of kinase-dead (KD) Pask, Wdr5WT or Wdr5S49A failed to induce MyoG expression (Figure 5H) in the same growth media condition.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 5H.

claims.claim: Wdr5 phosphorylation is a major mechanism whereby Pask promotes MyoG expression and myotube formation.
claims.source: Taken together, these data suggest that Wdr5 phosphorylation is a major mechanism whereby Pask promotes MyoG expression and myotube formation.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from all the Wdr5 rescue experiments.

claims.claim: At the onset of differentiation, the Myog promoter is remodeled with H3K4me3 modification resulting in its transcriptional activation.
claims.source: At the onset of differentiation, the Myog promoter is remodeled with H3K4me3 modification resulting in its transcriptional activation (Asp et al., 2011; Cheng et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Asp et al., 2011; Cheng et al., 2014).

claims.claim: The Myog locus contains a region of H3K4me3 approximately -150 bp upstream of the transcriptional start site (TSS), which overlaps with the peak of MyoD binding marked by E-Box sequences.
claims.source: The Myog locus contains a region of H3K4me3 approximately -150 bp upstream of the transcriptional start site (TSS), which overlaps with the peak of MyoD binding marked by E-Box sequences (Figure 6A).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 6A.

claims.claim: In control C2C12 cells, H3K4me3 abundance at two sites within the Myog promoter region (Myog_b and Myog_c) is strongly increased on Day 1 of differentiation, while a region more distal to the TSS shows little H3K4me3 accumulation (Myog_a).
claims.source: In control cells, H3K4me3 abundance at two sites within this region of the promoter (Myog_b and Myog_c) was strongly increased on Day 1 of differentiation, while a region more distal to the TSS showed little H3K4me3 accumulation (Myog_a, Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: The increase in H3K4me3 at the Myog promoter during differentiation is markedly blunted (Myog_b) or abolished (Myog_c) by Pask knockdown or inhibition.
claims.source: This increase in H3K4me3 was markedly blunted (Myog_b) or abolished (Myog_c) by Pask knockdown or inhibition (Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: Pask knockdown has no effect on H3K4me3 abundance on the Myod promoter.
claims.source: In contrast, Pask knockdown had no effect on H3K4me3 abundance on the Myod promoter (Figure 6B, Figure 6—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6B.

claims.claim: Expression of WT, but not KD, hPask completely rescues H3K4me3 occupancy of the Myog promoter in Pask knockdown cells.
claims.source: As we observed previously in microscopy experiments, expression of WT, but not KD, hPask completely rescued H3K4me3 occupancy of the Myog promoter (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Expression of Wdr5S49E restores H3K4me3 occupancy of the Myog promoter in Pask knockdown cells, whereas Wdr5S49A and Wdr5WT have no or modest effects, respectively.
claims.source: Moreover, expression of Wdr5S49E restored H3K4me3 occupancy, whereas Wdr5S49A and Wdr5WT had no or modest effects, respectively (Figure 6C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6C.

claims.claim: Wdr5WT modestly occupies the Myog promoter and this is decreased for the S49A mutant and increased for the S49E mutant.
claims.source: Consistent with that hypothesis, Wdr5WT modestly occupied the Myog promoter and this was decreased for the S49A mutant and increased for the S49E mutant (Figure 6D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Flag-Wdr5 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6D.

claims.claim: Neither WT nor KD Pask occupies the Myog promoter, consistent with the observation that Pask is not a stable member of any Wdr5-containing complexes.
claims.source: Neither WT nor KD Pask occupied the Myog promoter (Figure 6D), consistent with our observation that Pask is not a stable member of any Wdr5-containing complexes.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by Flag-Pask ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6D and represents an inference consistent with prior observations.

claims.claim: The increased binding of endogenous Wdr5 to the Myog promoter in response to differentiation cues observed in control cells is blunted in Pask-siRNA cells.
claims.source: We also examined the Pask-dependence of endogenous Wdr5 occupancy of the Myog promoter and found that the increased binding of Wdr5 to the Myog promoter in response to differentiation cues observed in control cells was blunted in Pask-siRNA cells (Figure 6E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by endogenous Wdr5 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: Wdr5 binding to the Myod promoter is neither significantly induced upon differentiation, nor is it affected by Pask knockdown.
claims.source: Wdr5 binding to the Myod promoter, on the other hand, was neither significantly induced upon differentiation, nor was it affected by Pask knockdown (Figure 6E), consistent with the observation that Pask is not required for expression of MyoD (Figure 2B, Figure 2—figure supplement 2D–E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by endogenous Wdr5 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6E.

claims.claim: MyoD is recruited to the Myog promoter during differentiation and then orchestrates the chromatin remodeling process to promote transcriptional activation of Myog.
claims.source: MyoD is recruited to the Myog promoter during differentiation and then in turn orchestrates the chromatin remodeling process to promote transcriptional activation of Myog (Palacios and Puri, 2006; Rampalli et al., 2007; Saccone and Puri, 2010).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Palacios and Puri, 2006; Rampalli et al., 2007; Saccone and Puri, 2010).

claims.claim: Pask knockdown completely blocks the differentiation-stimulated increase in MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that Pask knockdown completely blocked the differentiation-stimulated increase in MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter (Figure 6F, Figure 6—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by MyoD ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6F.

claims.claim: The requirement for Pask in MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter is due to Wdr5 phosphorylation as expression of Wdr5S49E increases MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter at Day 1 of differentiation, whereas Wdr5S49A blocks it.
claims.source: This requirement for Pask is due to Wdr5 phosphorylation as expression of Wdr5S49E increased MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter at Day 1 of differentiation, whereas Wdr5S49A blocked it (Figure 6G, Figure 6—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by MyoD ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: Wdr5S49E increases the MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter even in the absence of differentiation cues (Day 0) to a level similar to that found in control cells at Day 1 of differentiation.
claims.source: Interestingly, Wdr5S49E increased the MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter even in the absence of differentiation cues (Day 0) to a level similar to that found in control cells at Day 1 of differentiation (Figure 6G, Figure 6—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by MyoD ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 6G.

claims.claim: Pask and/or phospho-Wdr5 are necessary and sufficient to stimulate the myogenic transcriptional cascade.
claims.source: This result is consistent with our observation that Wdr5S49E expression is sufficient to induce MyoG expression in the absence of differentiation cues (Figure 5H). Thus, it appears that Pask and/or phospho-Wdr5 are necessary and sufficient to stimulate the myogenic transcriptional cascade, and perhaps that MyoD occupancy and H3K4me3 modification synergize to maximize expression from the Myog promoter during differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from the ChIP and expression data.

claims.claim: MyoD occupancy and H3K4me3 modification synergize to maximize expression from the Myog promoter during differentiation.
claims.source: Thus, it appears that Pask and/or phospho-Wdr5 are necessary and sufficient to stimulate the myogenic transcriptional cascade, and perhaps that MyoD occupancy and H3K4me3 modification synergize to maximize expression from the Myog promoter during differentiation.
claims.evidence: This claim is speculative inference from the data showing both factors are affected by Pask-Wdr5 signaling.

claims.claim: The Myog promoter has high H3K4me1 occupancy in non-differentiating C2C12 cells.
claims.source: The Myog promoter was recently shown to have high H3K4me1 occupancy in non-differentiating C2C12 cells (Cheng et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claims.claim: H3K4me1 marks on the Myog promoter are converted to H3K4me3 marks in response to differentiation cues through an unknown mechanism.
claims.source: These marks are converted to H3K4me3 marks in response to differentiation cues through an unknown mechanism (Cheng et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claims.claim: In control C2C12 cells, H3K4me1 marks are progressively depleted from the Myog promoter over the differentiation time-course, most likely due to further methylation to H3K4me3.
claims.source: In control cells, H3K4me1 marks were progressively depleted from the Myog promoter over the differentiation time-course (Figure 7A, Figure 7—source data 1), most likely due to further methylation to H3K4me3 (see Figure 6B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by H3K4me1 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7A and represents an inference based on the H3K4me3 data.

claims.claim: Pask knockdown severely blunts the loss of H3K4me1 from the Myog promoter during differentiation, in concert with blunting the appearance of H3K4me3.
claims.source: Pask knockdown severely blunted that loss of H3K4me1, in concert with blunting the appearance of H3K4me3 (Figure 7A, 6B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by H3K4me1 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7A.

claims.claim: H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion on the Myog promoter is accompanied by a decrease in total histone H3 density in control cells, suggestive of a transition from a transcriptionally inactive or closed (nucleosome rich) to a transcriptionally accessible or open (nucleosome depleted) state.
claims.source: This H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion was accompanied by a decrease in total histone H3 density at the Myog promoter in control cells (Figure 7B), suggestive of a transition from a transcriptionally inactive or closed (nucleosome rich) to a transcriptionally accessible or open (nucleosome depleted) state that might facilitate MyoD recruitment in control cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by total H3 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7B and represents an inference about chromatin state.

claims.claim: The loss of H3 density during differentiation is abolished by Pask knockdown.
claims.source: This loss of H3 density during differentiation was abolished by Pask knockdown (Figure 7B, Figure 7—source data 1).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by total H3 ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7B.

claims.claim: H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion at the Myog upstream enhancer is not impaired by Pask knockdown, nor is the appearance of H3K27ac.
claims.source: However, unlike the proximal Myog promoter, H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion at the Myog upstream enhancer is not impaired by Pask knockdown, nor is the appearance of H3K27ac (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B.

claims.claim: MyoD recruitment to the Myog enhancer during differentiation is impaired by Pask knockdown, possibly due to the interdependence of the enhancer and promoter for optimal activation.
claims.source: Interestingly, MyoD recruitment to the enhancer during differentiation is impaired similarly to the proximal promoter by Pask knockdown, possibly due to the interdependence of the enhancer and promoter for optimal activation (Sanyal et al., 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1B and citation to prior work (Sanyal et al., 2012), with speculation about the mechanism.

claims.claim: The Mybph and Acta1 promoters, but not Myod, undergo H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion during differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts and this is Pask-dependent.
claims.source: Like Myog, the Mybph and Acta1 promoters, but not Myod were reported to undergo H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion during differentiation in C2C12 myoblasts (Cheng et al., 2014) and this is also Pask-dependent (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C,D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C-D and citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Silencing of Mll3 at the onset of differentiation rescues the impaired Myog expression upon Pask knockdown.
claims.source: If the enhanced H3K4me1 occupancy at the Myog promoter is responsible for the transcriptional repression observed upon loss of Pask activity, then silencing of Mll3 at the onset of differentiation, which is specific for deposition of H3K4me1 marks might rescue the expression of Myog upon Pask knockdown. Indeed, we found that Mll3 knockdown in Pask-siRNA cells rescued the impaired Myog expression and restored differentiation as indicated by the Mylpf expression (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Mll3 knockdown in Pask-siRNA cells restores differentiation as indicated by Mylpf expression.
claims.source: Indeed, we found that Mll3 knockdown in Pask-siRNA cells rescued the impaired Myog expression and restored differentiation as indicated by the Mylpf expression (Figure 7C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 7C.

claims.claim: Pask is an essential mediator whereby differentiation cues stimulate H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion and chromatin remodeling to facilitate MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter.
claims.source: Taken together, our results show that Pask is an essential mediator whereby differentiation cues stimulate H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion and chromatin remodeling to facilitate MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from all the ChIP data showing Pask effects on histone marks and MyoD recruitment.

claims.claim: The requirement of Pask for loss of H3K4me1 and total H3 from the Myog promoter is related to Wdr5 phosphorylation since Wdr5S49E expression is sufficient to deplete H3K4me1 marks and total H3 occupancy on the Myog promoter even in the absence of differentiation cues.
claims.source: The requirement of Pask for loss of H3K4me1 and total H3 from the Myog promoter appears to be related to Wdr5 phosphorylation since Wdr5S49E expression was sufficient to deplete H3K4me1 marks (Figure 7D) and total H3 occupancy (Figure 7E) on the Myog promoter even in the absence of differentiation cues.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7D-E.

claims.claim: The depletion of H3K4me1 and total H3 at Day 1 of differentiation is prevented by the expression of Wdr5S49A.
claims.source: In contrast, the depletion of H3K4me1 and total H3 at Day 1 of differentiation was prevented by the expression of Wdr5S49A (Figure 7D,E).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-qPCR data shown in Figure 7D-E.

claims.claim: The effects of Wdr5S49A and Wdr5S49E expression on H3K4me1 and total H3 mirror those on MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter.
claims.source: These effects of Wdr5S49A and Wdr5S49E expression mirror those on MyoD occupancy of the Myog promoter (Figure 6G).
claims.evidence: This claim is an inference connecting the histone mark data with the MyoD recruitment data.

claims.claim: Wdr5 phosphorylation status dictates MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter, perhaps via H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion.
claims.source: Thus, Wdr5 phosphorylation status appears to dictate MyoD recruitment to the Myog promoter, perhaps via H3K4me1 to H3K4me3 conversion.
claims.evidence: This claim is a speculative inference about the mechanism linking Wdr5 phosphorylation to MyoD recruitment.

claims.claim: Pask-/- mice are developmentally normal despite the role of Pask in muscle regeneration response to injury in vivo.
claims.source: In spite of the role of Pask in the muscle regeneration response to injury in vivo that we have described, Pask-/- mice are developmentally normal.
claims.evidence: This claim is based on observation of the Pask-/- mouse phenotype.

claims.claim: The normal development of Pask-/- mice is similar to the phenotype of mice lacking the key myogenic transcription factors, Myod, Pax7, Myf5 or Mrf4.
claims.source: While surprising, this is similar to the phenotype of mice lacking the key myogenic transcription factors, Myod (Rudnicki et al., 1992), Pax7 (Seale et al., 2000), Myf5 (Kassar-Duchossoy et al., 2004; Kaul et al., 2000) or Mrf4 (Kassar-Duchossoy et al., 2004) (reviewed in (Musarò and 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work on myogenic transcription factor knockouts.

claims.claim: Myoblasts from Pask-/- mice have acquired resistance to Pask inhibitor-mediated suppression of myocyte differentiation, indicating that constitutive knockout results in a pro-differentiation compensatory response that is Pask-independent.
claims.source: Moreover, we found that myoblasts from Pask-/- mice had acquired resistance to Pask inhibitor-mediated suppression of myocyte differentiation, indicating that constitutive knockout results in a pro-differentiation compensatory response that is Pask-independent.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by the observation that BioE-1197 has no effect on Pask-/- myoblasts (Figure 1F-G).

claims.claim: Pask-siRNA or PASK-inhibited cells exhibit modest induction of Myog, its target genes and H3K4me3 abundance upon differentiation, suggesting the presence of Pask-independent mechanisms to drive myogenin induction.
claims.source: Similarly, Pask-siRNA or PASK-inhibited cells typically exhibited modest induction of Myog, its target genes and H3K4me3 abundance upon differentiation, suggesting the presence of Pask-independent mechanisms to drive myogenin induction.
claims.evidence: This claim is inferred from the observation that differentiation is impaired but not completely abolished by Pask loss.

claims.claim: Myf5 and other transcriptional regulators may drive some of the Pask-independent activation of the Myog promoter, as Pask-/- myoblasts exhibit elevated expression of Myf5.
claims.source: It's noteworthy that Pask-/- myoblasts exhibit elevated expression of Myf5 (Figure 2B), which has been shown to be able to compensate for the loss of MyoD function (Conerly et al., 2016; Rudnicki et al., 1992). Thus, it is possible that Myf5 and other transcriptional regulators drive some of the Pask-independent activation of the Myog promoter.
claims.evidence: This claim is speculative inference based on elevated Myf5 in Pask-/- cells and prior work showing Myf5 can compensate for MyoD.

claims.claim: The Pask-Wdr5 signaling axis is necessary and sufficient for full activation of the Myog promoter and subsequent myoblast fusion.
claims.source: Nonetheless, our data demonstrate that the Pask-Wdr5 signaling axis is necessary and sufficient for full activation of the Myog promoter and subsequent myoblast fusion.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary of the experimental findings showing Pask-Wdr5 effects on Myog expression and differentiation.

claims.claim: Pask expression is high in stem and progenitor cell types.
claims.source: We have shown that Pask expression is high in stem and progenitor cell types (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1A-C.

claims.claim: In ES cells, the Pask promoter is occupied by the pluripotency promoting transcription factors, Oct4 and Nanog.
claims.source: In ES cells, the Pask promoter is occupied by the pluripotency promoting transcription factors, Oct4 and Nanog (Figure 1—figure supplement 1D).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: Oct4 and Nanog transcription factor occupancy of the Pask promoter coincides with Pask transcriptional activation as indicated by the occupancy of RNA PolII as well as the activating H3K4me3 and H3K27ac chromatin modifications.
claims.source: This transcription factor occupancy coincided with the Pask transcriptional activation as indicated by the occupancy of RNA PolII as well as the activating H3K4me3 and H3K27ac chromatin modifications.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claims.claim: During muscle regeneration in vivo, Pask expression is dramatically induced as early as 3 days after injury, coincident with expansion of the satellite cell population and stimulation of MyoG expression.
claims.source: During muscle regeneration in vivo expression is dramatically induced as early as 3 days after injury (Figure 1H), coincident with expansion of the satellite cell population and stimulation of MyoG expression (Braun and Gautel, 2011).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1H and citation to prior work (Braun and Gautel, 2011).

claims.claim: MyoG and MyoD bind the Pask promoter.
claims.source: We showed that MyoG and MyoD bind the Pask promoter (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B), which is marked by broad domains of H3K4me3 occupancy similar to those found in other lineage-specifying genes (Benayoun et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 3A-B.

claims.claim: The Pask promoter is marked by broad domains of H3K4me3 occupancy similar to those found in other lineage-specifying genes.
claims.source: We showed that MyoG and MyoD bind the Pask promoter (Figure 2—figure supplement 3A–B), which is marked by broad domains of H3K4me3 occupancy similar to those found in other lineage-specifying genes (Benayoun et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by ChIP-Seq data and citation to prior work (Benayoun et al., 2014).

claims.claim: Terminal differentiation of ES cells and C2C12 myoblasts results in a decline in Pask expression, which ultimately reaches a low steady-state abundance when differentiation is complete.
claims.source: Terminal differentiation of ES cells and C2C12 myoblasts results in a decline in Pask expression, which ultimately reaches a low steady-state abundance when differentiation is complete.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by gene expression data from differentiation time courses.

claims.claim: The pattern of Pask expression is consistent with the expression of other key regulators of terminal differentiation like MyoD and hints at the importance of Pask in the lineage commitment process.
claims.source: This pattern is consistent with the expression of other key regulators of terminal differentiation like MyoD and hints at the importance of Pask in the lineage commitment process.
claims.evidence: This claim is an inference from the expression pattern of Pask.

claims.claim: Pharmacologic inhibition of Pask activity causes a loss of terminal differentiation in ES cells to a neuronal fate, C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal stem cells to adipocytes and C2C12 myoblasts to myotubes.
claims.source: Pharmacologic inhibition of Pask activity caused a loss of terminal differentiation in three differentiation paradigms: ES cells to a neuronal fate, C3H10T1/2 mesenchymal stem cells to adipocytes and C2C12 myoblasts to myotubes.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary of the differentiation experiments across multiple cell types.

claims.claim: Wdr5 has been previously implicated in controlling stem cell maintenance, with Oct4 associating with Wdr5 and recruiting H3K4me3 complexes to its target promoters to induce transcriptional activation and maintenance of pluripotency.
claims.source: Wdr5 has been previously implicated in controlling stem cell maintenance. For example, Oct4 associates with Wdr5 and recruits H3K4me3 complexes to its target promoters to induce transcriptional activation and maintenance of pluripotency (Ang et al., 2011).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Ang et al., 2011).

claims.claim: In C2C12 myoblasts, Wdr5 interacts with Pax7 to enforce myogenic specification.
claims.source: In C2C12 myoblasts, Wdr5 was shown to interact with Pax7 to enforce myogenic specification (Kawabe et al., 2012; McKinnell et al., 2008; Rudnicki et al., 2008).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Kawabe et al., 2012; McKinnell et al., 2008; Rudnicki et al., 2008).

claims.claim: The results provide a new regulatory role for Wdr5 in promoting differentiation via the expression of key target genes.
claims.source: Our results provide a new regulatory role for Wdr5 in promoting differentiation via the expression of key target genes.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from the experimental findings.

claims.claim: The results define a novel regulatory paradigm wherein the function of Wdr5 is modulated by Pask-dependent phosphorylation.
claims.source: More importantly, these results define a novel regulatory paradigm wherein the function of Wdr5 is modulated by Pask-dependent phosphorylation.
claims.evidence: This claim is a summary inference from the experimental findings showing Pask phosphorylates Wdr5 to regulate its function.

claims.claim: It is likely, but remains to be established, whether Wdr5 phosphorylation is a conserved and required mechanism whereby Pask promotes the differentiation of other stem and progenitor cells.
claims.source: While we deem it likely, it remains to be established whether Wdr5 phosphorylation is a conserved and required mechanism whereby Pask promotes the differentiation of other stem and progenitor cells.
claims.evidence: This claim is speculation about the generalizability of the findings.

claims.claim: Differentiation cues engage and activate the signaling pathways and transcriptional networks that combine to drive terminal differentiation.
claims.source: Differentiation cues engage and activate the signaling pathways and transcriptional networks that combine to drive terminal differentiation (Basson, 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Basson, 2012) and represents established knowledge.

claims.claim: While a pioneering transcription factor like MyoD can occupy its target promoters in a sequence-specific manner, the full activation of the MyoD transcriptional response depends upon signaling from differentiation cues.
claims.source: While a pioneering transcription factor like MyoD can occupy its target promoters in a sequence-specific manner, the full activation of the MyoD transcriptional response depends upon signaling from differentiation cues (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005).

claims.claim: Differentiation cues are thought to enhance MyoD binding to its target promoters and recruit histone modifying proteins to initiate the expression of differentiation genes.
claims.source: These cues, including those used in vitro treatment with insulin, are thought to enhance MyoD binding to its target promoters and recruit histone modifying proteins to initiate the expression of differentiation genes (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005; Blum and Dynlacht, 2013; Braun and Gautel, 2011; Dilworth and Blais, 2011).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Berkes and Tapscott, 2005; Blum and Dynlacht, 2013; Braun and Gautel, 2011; Dilworth and Blais, 2011).

claims.claim: Ectopic expression of Pask or phospho-mimetic Wdr5 is sufficient to induce MyoD binding to target promoters, recruitment of histone modifying proteins, and myogenic gene expression in the absence of differentiation cues.
claims.source: Ectopic expression of Pask or phospho-mimetic Wdr5 was sufficient to induce all of these effects in the absence of differentiation cues (Figure 2K–J, Figure 5H).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 2K-J and 5H.

claims.claim: Pask might be a critical node in the signaling network connecting differentiation cues with myogenic gene expression.
claims.source: These data raise the possibility that Pask might be a critical node in the signaling network connecting differentiation cues with myogenic gene expression.
claims.evidence: This claim is speculative inference from the sufficiency of Pask to induce differentiation.

claims.claim: Pask activity and the Pask-Wdr5 interaction are stimulated by differentiation cues.
claims.source: Consistent with that hypothesis, we found that Pask activity was stimulated by differentiation cues as was the Pask-Wdr5 interaction (Figure 4F).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by kinase assay and co-immunoprecipitation data shown in Figure 4F and 4A.

claims.claim: Differentiation cues act, at least in part, to drive the myogenic transcriptional program via Pask activation and phosphorylation of Wdr5.
claims.source: We therefore believe that differentiation cues act, at least in part, to drive the myogenic transcriptional program via Pask activation and phosphorylation of Wdr5.
claims.evidence: This claim is an inference from the data showing Pask is activated by differentiation cues and phosphorylates Wdr5 to promote differentiation.

claims.claim: It remains unknown how Pask activity and the Pask-Wdr5 interaction are stimulated by differentiation cues.
claims.source: It remains unknown how Pask activity and the Pask-Wdr5 interaction are stimulated by differentiation cues, but we suggest that these phenomena are likely central components of this signaling pathway.
claims.evidence: This claim acknowledges a gap in knowledge while speculating about importance.

claims.claim: H3K4me1 was recently demonstrated to be a transcriptionally repressive mark at the promoters of myogenic genes.
claims.source: H3K4me1 was recently demonstrated to be a transcriptionally repressive mark at the promoters of myogenic genes (Cheng et al., 2014).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claims.claim: In response to differentiation cues, H3K4me1 is further methylated to H3K4me3 on myogenic promoters to initiate their expression.
claims.source: In response to differentiation cues, H3K4me1 is further methylated to H3K4me3 on these promoters to initiate their expression.
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Cheng et al., 2014).

claims.claim: H3K4 monomethylation is catalyzed by the Wdr5-containing Mll3/Mll4 complexes.
claims.source: H3K4 monomethylation is catalyzed by the Wdr5-containing Mll3/Mll4 complexes (Hu et al., 2013), while the Wdr5-containing Mll1/Mll2 complexes catalyze H3K4 trimethylation (Shilatifard, 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior work (Hu et al., 2013; Shilatifard, 2012).

claims.claim: The Wdr5-containing Mll1/Mll2 complexes catalyze H3K4 trimethylation.
claims.source: H3K4 monomethylation is catalyzed by the Wdr5-containing Mll3/Mll4 complexes (Hu et al., 2013), while the Wdr5-containing Mll1/Mll2 complexes catalyze H3K4 trimethylation (Shilatifard, 2012).
claims.evidence: This claim is supported by citation to prior work (Shilatifard, 2012).

claims.claim: It has been predicted that differentiation cues promote a Mll3/Mll4 to Mll1/Mll2 switch on myogenic promoters via an unknown mechanism.
